title: Theory of Computer Science
description: Starter practice for regular languages and finite automata.

questions.question: Which operation is part of the inductive definition of regular languages?
questions.explanation: Regular languages are closed under operations including union, concatenation, and Kleene star.

questions.question: Why is the language described by [A-Z][0-9][A-Z][0-9][A-Z][0-9] finite?
options: Every word has a fixed length and every position has finitely many choices
All regular expressions describe finite languages
questions.explanation: There are six fixed positions and each position draws from a finite set.

questions.question: What does the Kleene star L* include for every language L?
questions.explanation: Zero repetitions are allowed, so epsilon is always in L*.

questions.question: What information must a DFA use to decide its next state?
options: Its current state and current input symbol
Only the length of the input
questions.explanation: A DFA transition is determined by exactly one current state and one input symbol.

questions.question: A DFA recognizing binary strings whose number of 1s is a multiple of three naturally tracks what?
questions.explanation: Three states can represent remainders 0, 1, and 2 modulo three.

questions.question: What is the core idea of subset construction?
options: Turn each DFA state into a symbol
Represent a DFA state as a set of possible NFA states
Replace transitions with regular expressions only
questions.explanation: Each constructed DFA state records all NFA states reachable after reading the same input.

questions.question: To disprove a universal claim, what is normally sufficient?
questions.explanation: A single case satisfying the premise but violating the conclusion refutes a universal statement.

questions.question: Which models recognize exactly the regular languages?
questions.explanation: DFAs, NFAs, and regular expressions have equivalent expressive power.
